items.text: What is the maximum diameter of a bored hole in a sawn floor joist?
C. One-third of the joist depth — R502.8.1 limits bored holes in sawn joists to D/3; D/6 is the notch limit and D/4 is the end-notch limit.
How far must a bored hole in a joist be kept from the top or bottom edge, from any other hole, and from any notch?
A. At least 2 inches — R502.8.1 requires 2 inches minimum clearance from the hole to the joist edges, to any other hole, and to any notch.
A carpenter notches the end of a sawn joist directly over its bearing. What is the maximum notch depth?
B. One-fourth of the joist depth — R502.8.1 allows end notches over the bearing up to D/4 - deeper than the D/6 limit that applies in the outer thirds of the span.
A 2 by 10 joist has an actual depth of nine and one-quarter inches. What is the largest hole a plumber may bore through it?
D. Three and one-sixteenth inches — Per R502.8.1 the hole limit is D/3: 9-1/4 inches divided by 3 is about 3-1/16 inches; 1-17/32 is the D/6 notch and 2-5/16 the D/4 end notch.
A framer wants to notch the flange of a wood I-joist to clear a pipe. What does the code say?

B. Prohibited unless the manufacturer's literature permits it or a registered design professional evaluates it — R502.8.2 prohibits cuts, notches, and holes in trusses, LVL, glulam, and I-joists except where the manufacturer permits or a registered design professional approves.
How is a built-up girder of 2-inch nominal lumber nailed together?

A. 20d nails at 32 inches on center top and bottom staggered, with two 20d at ends and splices — Table R602.3(1) requires built-up girders to be nailed with 20d common nails at 32 inches o.c. top and bottom staggered, plus two 20d at ends and at each splice.
The end of a wood girder enters a masonry wall pocket. What protection is required?
C. A one-half inch air space on the top, sides, and end of the girder — R502.6.1 requires a 1/2-inch air space on the top, sides, and end where wood girders enter masonry walls, for decay protection.
A stair opening in a floor requires a header joist spanning 5 feet. What framing does R502.10 require?

D. Double the header joist and double the trimmer joists — R502.10 requires doubling both the header joist and the trimmer joists when the header span exceeds 4 feet; hangers are triggered above 6 feet.
At what header joist span in a floor opening do approved hangers become required?
A. When the header span exceeds 6 feet — R502.10 requires approved hangers where the header joist span exceeds 6 feet; the 4-foot threshold is where doubling begins.
Double joists under a parallel bearing partition are separated to allow piping. What does R502.4 require?

B. Full-depth solid blocking of 2-inch nominal lumber at not more than 4 feet on center — R502.4 requires full-depth solid blocking not less than 2-inch nominal at intervals of 4 feet o.c. or less when doubled joists are separated for piping or vents.
Without an engineered design or a code table, how far may a 2 by 10 floor joist cantilever beyond its support?

C. About 10 inches - not more than the nominal depth of the joist — R502.3.3 limits prescriptive floor cantilevers to the nominal depth of the joist; the L/4 rule is a 2021 IRC deck provision not in the 2015 MRC.
What is the maximum spacing of 2 by 4 bearing studs supporting one floor plus a roof-ceiling?
B. 16 inches on center — Table R602.3(5) allows 2x4 bearing studs supporting one floor plus roof-ceiling at 16 inches o.c.; 24 inches o.c. applies when supporting roof-ceiling only.
A bearing wall must support two floors plus a roof-ceiling. What stud arrangement does the 2015 MRC allow prescriptively?
D. 2 by 6 studs at 16 inches on center — Table R602.3(5) requires 2x6 studs at 16 inches o.c. for walls supporting two floors plus a roof - 2x4 studs are not permitted prescriptively for that load.
In a double top plate, how far must end joints be offset from each other?
A. At least 24 inches — R602.3.2 requires double top plates to be overlapped at corners and intersections with end joints offset at least 24 inches.
A single top plate is used instead of a double top plate. What splice does the exception in R602.3.2 require at joints?

C. A 3 by 6 inch galvanized splice plate of 20-gage steel with six 8d nails on each side — R602.3.2 allows a single top plate only with a 3x6-inch, 0.036-inch (20-gage) galvanized splice plate fastened with six 8d nails each side, with joists or rafters within 1 inch of stud centers.
What is the maximum notch in a stud in a load-bearing exterior wall?
B. 25 percent of the stud width — R602.6 limits notches in bearing and exterior wall studs to 25 percent of the stud width; 40 percent is the nonbearing notch limit.
What is the maximum bored hole in a stud in a nonbearing partition?
D. 60 percent of the stud width — R602.6 allows bored holes up to 60 percent of the stud width in nonbearing partitions (or in doubled bearing studs); 40 percent is the single bearing-stud limit.
How close may the edge of a bored hole in a stud come to the edge of the stud?
A. No closer than five-eighths inch — R602.6 requires the edge of a bored hole to be at least 5/8 inch from the edge of the stud, and the hole may not share a cross-section with a notch.
A braced wall panel must begin within what distance of each end of a braced wall line?

C. Within 10 feet — R602.10.2.2 requires a braced wall panel to begin within 10 feet of each end of the braced wall line, with not more than 20 feet between adjacent panel edges - 12 feet 6 inches is a 2021-era trap.
In the wall bracing methods, what does WSP stand for and what is its minimum panel thickness?
B. Wood structural panel, three-eighths inch — R602.10 method WSP is wood structural panel bracing with a minimum thickness of 3/8 inch, and it needs shorter total bracing lengths than LIB or GB.
Ceiling joists run perpendicular to the rafters and cannot resist thrust. What does R802.3.1 require?

A. Rafter ties of at least 2 by 4 installed in the lower part of the attic — R802.3.1 requires rafter ties of at least 2x4 in the lower part of the attic where ceiling joists do not resist thrust; otherwise the ridge must be a designed beam.
Where ceiling joists are lapped over a bearing wall, what is the minimum lap?
D. 3 inches — R802.3.2 requires ceiling joists to be lapped a minimum of 3 inches or butted over the bearing and toenailed to the bearing member.
How must purlin braces be installed under a purlin supporting rafters?

C. 2 by 4 braces at not less than 45 degrees, not more than 4 feet on center, unbraced length not over 8 feet — R802.5.1 requires purlins braced to bearing walls with 2x4 braces at 45 degrees or steeper, spaced 4 feet o.c. or less, with an unbraced brace length of 8 feet or less; the purlin itself must be at least the size of the rafters it supports.
What is the minimum nominal thickness of a valley or hip rafter?
B. 2 inch nominal — R802.3 requires valley and hip rafters to be at least 2-inch nominal thickness and not less in depth than the cut end of the rafter; the 1-inch value is for the ridge board.
Per the fastening schedule, how is one top plate nailed to the plate below?

A. 16d common nails at 16 inches on center, face nailed — Table R602.3(1) requires top plate to top plate fastening with 16d common nails at 16 inches o.c., face nailed; the double top plate splice takes 8-16d each side of the joint.
How is a collar tie fastened to a rafter per the fastening schedule?
D. Three 10d common face nails, or a 20-gage ridge strap — Table R602.3(1) requires collar ties fastened with three 10d common face nails, or a 1-1/4 inch 20-gage ridge strap may be used instead.
What is the required nailing pattern for wood structural panel wall sheathing three-eighths to one-half inch thick?

C. 6 inches on center at panel edges, 12 inches on center in the field — Table R602.3(1) requires WSP sheathing nailed at 6 inches o.c. along panel edges and 12 inches o.c. at intermediate (field) supports.
Where a deck lateral load connection is provided under R507.2.3, what is required?

A. Hold-down tension devices at two or more locations, each with a 1,500 pound capacity — R507.2.3 requires hold-down tension devices at not fewer than 2 locations per deck with a capacity of 1,500 pounds each.
A builder is digging footings for an attached deck in Michigan. What minimum depth applies?
D. 42 inches - the Michigan frost depth, same as the house — The Michigan amendment to R403.1.4 sets frost depth at 42 inches, and deck footings follow the same rule as the house foundation.
At what height range must a stair handrail be mounted above the nosings?
B. 34 to 38 inches — R311.7.8 requires handrails between 34 and 38 inches above the nosings, and a handrail is required on stairways with 4 or more risers.
